summary: Moving grouped-MoE routing metadata fully onto the GPU preserved correctness and removed a synchronization hazard, but the matched batch-2 campaign still measured about 59% median utilization. Metadata placement alone was not the utilization root cause.
title: GPU routing metadata was necessary but insufficient

summary: At sequence 2048 with the same global batch, increasing the physical microbatch from 2 to 4 and reducing accumulation from 8 to 4 raised median throughput to 10,911.78 tokens/s and median GPU utilization to 87%, with 9.83 GiB peak allocated VRAM. The earlier low utilization was not inherent to KDA or MoE.
title: Physical microbatch geometry repairs most utilization loss

summary: Disabling activation checkpointing at batch 2 produced a 12,440.09 tokens/s median control at about 68% median utilization, but consumed roughly 10.30 GiB peak allocated VRAM and approached the physical device limit. Recomputation geometry is a major throughput axis and needs segment sweeps plus stability validation rather than blanket removal.
title: Recomputation policy is a first-order systems variable

summary: The historical 12.3k-14.2k tokens/s screens used a 415.7M standard MoE without activation checkpointing and with APOLLO, whereas the current K3 proxy is a 269.7M total, 188.3M active latent-MoE model with per-block checkpointing and AdamW. Those results are useful system references but are not direct same-model regressions.
title: Old and current throughput screens are not directly comparable

summary: A full diagnostic with checkpoint segment size 2 at batch 4 reached 13.32 GiB allocator peak on the 12 GiB RTX 4080 Laptop GPU, reported 100 percent utilization, and collapsed to 948 tokens per second. The run was not clean-source promotion evidence because a flattened bash launcher imported the main checkout. A corrected source-pinned repeat was intentionally aborted to avoid wasting roughly 17 minutes per repetition. Per-block recomputation remains the usable policy pending a redesigned TE-aware segment path.
title: Multi-block TE recomputation thrashes laptop VRAM

summary: A clean-commit batch-4 screen at 2,048 tokens with segment size 2 and reentrant Transformer Engine checkpointing sustained 11,272.92 median tokens/s at 85.5% median GPU utilization with 3.95 GiB peak allocated VRAM. The prior non-reentrant diagnostic reached 13.32 GiB allocator peak and collapsed to 948 tokens/s. Multi-block recomputation is viable when TE saves only segment inputs; the architecture was not intrinsically slow.
title: Input-only TE recomputation fixes segment memory thrash

summary: Clean-commit batch-4 screens at 2,048 tokens measured 11,272.92 tokens/s and 3.95 GiB peak for segment 2, 11,657.996 tokens/s and 4.98 GiB for segment 4, and 11,397.21 tokens/s and 7.26 GiB for segment 8. Segment 4 also reached 90% median GPU utilization. It is the provisional recomputation Pareto point pending a longer two-repetition confirmation.
title: Four-block input-only recomputation leads the short screen

summary: A clean-commit two-repetition confirmation at batch 4 and sequence 2,048 measured 10,815.07 tokens/s, 84% median GPU utilization, and 4.98 GiB median peak allocation for four-block reentrant Transformer Engine checkpointing. The independent repetition medians were 11,153.08 and 10,477.07 tokens/s, so the earlier 11,658 tokens/s short screen was directionally correct but optimistic. Segment 4 is the current laptop execution default because it preserves substantial VRAM headroom while sustaining high utilization; long-context geometry still requires separate validation.
title: Four-block input-only recomputation is the confirmed laptop default

summary: The first 1,048,576-token matched quality smoke recorded a clean campaign start at commit 16921f4, but candidate subprocesses imported the mutable main checkout. The K3 reference process therefore loaded later uncommitted evaluation-role code and failed after completing evaluation because the console formatter assumed every metric was numeric. Dense, KDA and K3 losses remain diagnostic only; the campaign is not promotion evidence. The runner now executes every subprocess from a verified detached commit worktree with absolute external data/config paths.
title: Mutable subprocess source invalidated the first matched quality smoke

summary: The first detached-source matched 1,048,576-token smoke at seed 1337 completed all four runs. Dense MLA reached validation loss 6.63863, dense KDA3+MLA 7.55976, K3 latent-MoE BF16 reference 7.52083, and the K3 CUTLASS FP8 system recipe 7.52909. K3 is slightly ahead of dense KDA3 at this scale but both trail dense MLA materially. This is valid early learning evidence, not an architecture verdict: one seed, one validation batch, very short training, unmatched parameter counts, and no long-context retrieval yet.
title: Dense MLA leads the first valid 1M-token quality smoke

summary: On the same K3 architecture/data/seed, the CUTLASS plus Transformer Engine FP8 surroundings measured 3,367.47 median tokens/s and 7.52909 validation loss versus 2,532.90 tokens/s and 7.52083 for the BF16 per-expert reference: 32.95 percent higher throughput, 0.00826 higher loss, and 26.34 percent lower training wall time. Mean utilization was only 43.17 percent because this quality recipe uses microbatch 1; it is not a ceiling and must not supersede the separate batch-4 segment-4 system result. Because precision and surrounding linears differ, this is a system-recipe result, not pure kernel numerical parity; a BF16 CUTLASS control is running.
title: CUTLASS plus FP8 surroundings improves the microbatch-1 MoE recipe

summary: A detached-source 1,048,576-token BF16 CUTLASS run used the identical K3 model-config hash and bf16-torch numerical family as the BF16 per-expert reference. It reached validation loss 7.52353 versus 7.52083, an absolute delta of 0.00270, while median training throughput rose from 2,532.90 to 4,029.04 tokens/s (1.5907x), wall time fell from 397.39 to 243.62 seconds, and mean utilization rose from 40.67 to 47.33 percent in the deliberately small microbatch-1 quality recipe. Seven direct CUDA grouped-MoE parity/switch/alignment tests also passed. This confirms a narrow numerical/learning parity smoke and a material execution improvement; it does not yet promote the autotune cache or replace the batch-4 segment-4 throughput result, because longer multi-seed quality and exact final-run geometry remain required.
title: BF16 CUTLASS preserves the K3 smoke trajectory at 1.59x reference throughput
